prompt:
Here is a problem from another field that shares the underlying structure of the research question below, with notes on how that field investigates it.

<parallel>
Field: Materials science (metallurgy)
Problem: Determining whether a shape-memory alloy's or metal's microstructure (e.g., dislocation networks) stores a record of past deformation that shapes its future response, once the original stress is gone.
How it is studied: Researchers run cyclic loading and thermal cycling tests and compare hysteresis loops between pre-treated and virgin samples. They use electron microscopy and X-ray diffraction to map the stored microstructure. Annealing experiments check how much heat is needed to erase the memory, which shows whether the structure itself is the carrier.
</parallel>

Each of your ideas must transfer a specific method, measurement logic, or principle from how that field studies its problem, while still being a concrete, scientifically sound way to address the research question.

Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Primed vs. virgin hysteresis comparison
ideas.description: Pre-stimulate cells (e.g., with EGF, TPA, or a cytokine), withdraw the stimulus for varied rest periods, then restimulate and compare dose-response and induction-kinetics curves of AP-1 target genes against naive cells. Differences in amplitude, threshold, or speed of the second response, plotted as a loop across stimulus history, quantify memory.

ideas.title: Chromatin-state mapping of the stored record
ideas.description: Use ATAC-seq, CUT&RUN/ChIP for FOS/JUN, H3K27ac, and BAF remodeler marks, plus footprinting, in primed, rested, and naive cells to see whether AP-1-bound enhancers remain open after the signal is gone. Persistent accessibility at AP-1 motifs that correlates with enhanced re-induction, analogous to imaging dislocation networks, would identify the structural carrier.

ideas.title: Annealing-style erasure titration
ideas.description: Test how much perturbation is needed to erase memory: dose-titrate inhibitors of chromatin remodeling (BRG1/SWI-SNF), histone acetyltransferases, or DNA replication/cell divisions, and measure when the primed response reverts to naive. If memory decays only with disruption of AP-1-dependent chromatin and not with loss of AP-1 protein levels, the chromatin structure rather than ongoing AP-1 activity carries the record.

ideas.title: Acute AP-1 degradation at different time windows
ideas.description: Use degron-tagged (dTAG/AID) JUN/FOS or dominant-negative A-FOS to remove AP-1 either during priming, during the rest period, or during restimulation, then read out the secondary response. Distinguishing a requirement for writing the memory from maintaining or reading it shows whether AP-1 is the carrier or just an initiator.

ideas.title: Single-cell and lineage-tracked history–response mapping
ideas.description: Combine live reporters of AP-1 activity (FOS/JUN dynamics) with single-cell RNA/ATAC-seq and lineage tracing across divisions to relate each cell's past AP-1 dynamics to its later response. Heritability of response across sister cells and its decay over generations tests whether memory is cell-intrinsic and stable, as opposed to residual signaling.
